blog_summary: The blog post highlights a novel approach to live migration of web workers in mobile applications, enabling seamless offloading of computation from mobile devices to edge clouds. Adrian Colyer emphasizes the elegance of leveraging the HTML5 Web Worker interface for this purpose, as workers are designed for separate-thread execution via message passing, making them ideal for migration. The paper addresses the challenge of snapshotting complex worker states, including JavaScript objects, WebAssembly functions, and native objects, while ensuring compatibility across different hardware architectures (e.g., ARM to x86). The Mobile Web Worker (MWW) System dynamically selects the optimal execution location (local device, edge, or cloud) based on predicted latency and connectivity, using regression models to estimate processing time. The system also handles disconnections by migrating workers to fallback servers or back to the client. The prototype, implemented in Chrome and Node.js, demonstrates significant performance improvements for applications like physics simulations, face detection, and image filtering, with edge offloading yielding up to 2.6x speedups. However, migration times vary widely depending on state size, with larger states (e.g., OpenCV) taking several seconds to migrate.
paper_title: Seamless offloading of web app computations from mobile device to edge clouds via HTML5 web worker migration
